memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So Moses spoke to the Israelites, and their leaders gave him twelve staffs, one for the leader of each of their ancestral tribes, and Aaron's staff was among them. Moses placed the staffs before the Lord in the tent of the covenant law. The next day Moses entered the tent and saw that Aaron's staff, which represented the tribe of Levi, had not only sprouted but had budded, blossomed and produced almonds. — Num 17:6-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The result is beyond anything the people could have argued their way to. Aaron's staff had not merely sprouted a single reluctant bud. It "had budded, blossomed and produced almonds" — the whole cycle of life, from bud to blossom to ripe fruit, all in a single night. God's answer was not a faint hint but an overflowing, unmistakable display.

Notice the abundance. God could have made the staff show one small green shoot, just enough to prove His point. Instead He gave buds and blossoms and mature fruit all at once. When God confirms something, He does it generously. His answers often exceed what we ask or expect, not because we deserve it, but because He is lavish in His grace.

There is beauty, too, in the choice of an almond branch. The almond was among the first trees to bloom each spring, an early sign of new life after winter. Through this ancient, blossoming staff, God was speaking of life, of fruitfulness, of His power to make the barren flourish. What the other eleven staffs could not do, God did through the one He had chosen.

This points us gently toward Christ. Aaron's fruitful staff marked out God's chosen priest; and Jesus is the true and eternal High Priest whom God has chosen and confirmed. He is the branch that bears everlasting fruit, the one through whom life comes to the barren. Apart from Him we are like the eleven lifeless staffs; joined to Him, we blossom and bear fruit that lasts. Abide in Him, and let His life flow through you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have you seen God's answers exceed what you expected?
2. What does it mean that fruitfulness comes only through God's chosen One?
3. How can you abide more closely in Christ, the true living branch?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that when You confirm Your purposes, You do it abundantly. Thank You for Jesus, the true branch through whom life and fruit come. Help me to abide in Him, that my life may blossom and bear lasting fruit. Amen.
